newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault may accelerate plant closure - paper.
newsitem.headline: Renault may accelerate plant closure - paper.

text.p: Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer said in a newspaper interview published on Friday that the carmaker may close the Vilvoorde assembly plant before July 31 if its workers do not resume production.

"If the plant doesn't start up, we risk not being able to use the advisory period and declare the declare the closure before July 31," he told the newspaper Liberation. Renault in February said it wanted to close the plant by the end of July.
A Belgian court ruled on Thursday that the French company violated labour rules in announcing the closure, but Renault said the ruling did not alter its intentions.

Workers have halted production at Vilvoorde since the announcement on February 27 of the closure. Schweitzer recently indicated that the company was flexible on the July 31 deadline and could keep the plant open weeks or even months longer though it expected a closure by year's end.

Asked why Renault had not adopted a strategy similar to that of Volkswagen, which reduced employees' hours, Schweitzer told Liberation, "Reducing work time and wages would not have saved Vilvoorde. Beyond job reductions, we have an industrial problem. We had to cut one assembly site..."
He said the average age of workers at Vilvoorde -- 38 compared with over 40 for the company as a whole -- did not allow for a gradual winding down through early retirements.
Schweitzer said Renault had been in contact with potential buyers of the site. "But do you really think that with the present situation that would make any sense?"
Renault has said it would seek a buyer for Vilvoorde and sell the plant for a nominal sum.

Schweitzer said the French government's continued presence as a major shareholder -- it owns 46 percent of Renault -- had clouded the issue, as the company is still perceived as partly state-run by the public and by Belgian authorities. He said he wanted to see the state reduce its stake soon.
